subject.title: Renderer placeholder leak: `(see attached image)`, `Image reply`, `Audio reply`, `Media reply` leak to human-visible Telegram reply under specific content-classification paths

question: Should the Telegram/reply-media owners authorize an instrumented live trace through normalization and the final Telegram send boundary before any repair is scoped?
rationale: The report is detailed, but the proposed literal replacement is unsafe and current source does not establish that prompt or transcript placeholders become the Telegram payload; owner-guided instrumentation is needed to identify the responsible boundary.

options.title: Run boundary trace
options.body: Capture redacted pre-normalization, post-normalization, and Telegram Bot API payloads for one media-only reply-directive turn, then scope the fix from the first incorrect transition.

options.title: Request reporter payload
options.body: Keep the issue blocked until the reporter supplies redacted gateway logs or a Bot API payload showing the placeholder in the outbound request.

options.title: Treat as prompt-only overlap
options.body: Close or redirect only if maintainers confirm the observed behavior is fully explained by the model-visible problem tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99241.

recommendation.title: Run boundary trace
recommendation.body: Capture redacted pre-normalization, post-normalization, and Telegram Bot API payloads for one media-only reply-directive turn, then scope the fix from the first incorrect transition.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to recently proven Telegram-visible rendering and delivery behavior.
